context: Harbor account recovery playbook. A customer who loses a recovery device should open a recovery request from the public help page. The form asks for a workspace name and a contact address. It does not ask for a password, a recovery code, a card number, or an identity document. Support sends the request identifier to the supplied contact address. Receiving this identifier confirms receipt of the request; it does not establish account ownership. An assigned reviewer then checks the request against the workspace's recovery contacts. Only contacts already registered in the workspace can confirm the request through this process. A newly supplied email address is a contact destination, not a replacement for a registered recovery contact. If no registered recovery contact can be reached, the reviewer records that the request needs an alternative verification path and leaves access unchanged. The reviewer must not promise that the account will be restored. If verification succeeds, the reviewer sends a temporary sign-in link to a registered recovery contact. The link expires after 20 minutes and can be used once. Creating a new link invalidates an older unused link for the same request. After signing in, the customer must register a replacement recovery device before closing the request. Support records the verification decision and whether the replacement device was registered. The request can be closed only after that device registration is confirmed. The playbook gives no maximum completion time, because reviewer availability and the ability to reach registered contacts vary. It offers no paid priority lane. A workspace administrator can view the status of a recovery request but cannot bypass verification. Status messages must distinguish receipt, pending verification, successful verification, and closure. None of these messages should imply that a step occurred merely because a customer asked for it.
